conversation.content:
Good morning, Ms. Lopez. I’m Dr. Ramirez, a perinatal-mental-health clinician here to support new mothers in the weeks and months after birth. Today I’ll be using a short, well-studied questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)** to check in on how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically during this postpartum period. It’s simply a way to open the conversation—nothing you share will leave this room without your permission, and there are no “right” or “wrong” answers. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days; each one usually takes just a moment. I’ll ask them conversationally, and you can tell me whatever feels true for you.

Whenever you’re ready, we can start.  

First, thinking about the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?
Honestly? Not much. I can crack a smile if my husband pulls a silly face, but it feels forced—like I’m going through the motions. Most jokes just fall flat for me lately.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes, but not really. I’ll force a little laugh if my husband tries to be goofy, but it feels fake and disappears right away. Nothing feels genuinely funny inside.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels flat. I’ll plan something, hoping it’ll lift me up, and then when the time comes I’m just… meh, like the color’s drained out of it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… more than I’d like to admit. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, my head jumps straight to “I’m doing something wrong” or “I’m not a good enough mom.” I’ll replay every little thing I did and pick it apart, even when people tell me it’s normal newborn stuff.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. My mind keeps spinning with “what-ifs” about the baby—like what if he stops breathing in the night, or what if I’m missing some sign that he’s sick. There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just pop in and I can’t shut them off for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes it hits out of nowhere—my heart races, I feel shaky, and for a minute I’m sure something awful is about to happen, even though I can’t name what. It fades after a bit, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah, a lot of the time. It feels like there’s this never-ending pile of baby stuff, house stuff, and my own thoughts all stacked up, and I can’t see the top. Some mornings I wake up already exhausted, thinking, “How am I going to get through today?” I still push through for the baby, but it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling through worries about the baby and all the ways I’m probably messing up. I’ll drift off eventually, then wake up again with my heart pounding for no clear reason. It’s been like that several nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most days, yeah. It’s like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll be feeding the baby or folding laundry and just feel tears behind my eyes for no single reason. The sadness isn’t every single minute, but it’s definitely there more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened a couple of times this week. Once was after I finally got him down for a nap—should feel like a win, right? Instead I sat on the couch and just burst into tears. Another night I cried quietly while pumping because everything felt so heavy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… the thought has flickered through my mind once or twice. Nothing planned—just this quick, scary image of “what if I weren’t here.” It makes me feel awful for even thinking it, and I push it away fast, but it’s shown up.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary**  
*Patient*: Postpartum mother, ≤1 yr post-delivery

**Presenting Concerns**  
- Persistent low mood, described as “gray cloud,” present “most days”  
- Marked anhedonia: unable to anticipate or experience pleasure from previously enjoyable activities  
- Daily, intrusive “what-if” worries about infant safety; episodes of panic (racing heart, shakiness) without clear trigger  
- Pronounced guilt / self-blame regarding infant care (“I’m not a good enough mom”)  
- Frequent tearfulness, including at times infant is settled; described as feeling “heavy”  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia driven by ruminative worries; wakes with heart pounding  
- Overwhelm / feeling “barely treading water” with daily tasks  
- Passive self-harm ideation (fleeting thoughts of “what if I weren’t here”) without plan or intent

**Pattern Summary**  
Symptoms cluster around depressive (mood, pleasure, guilt, crying, sleep) and anxiety (excessive worry, panic) domains; functional impairment evident in self-care and parenting confidence.

**Screening Significance / Risk Flags**  
- Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale proxy: positive indicators on items consistent with probable major depression + comorbid anxiety  
- Safety concern: presence of any self-harm thoughts → warrants immediate safety assessment

**Recommendation for Next Step**  
Urgent referral for comprehensive perinatal mental health evaluation, safety planning, and consideration of evidence-based intervention (psychotherapy and/or medication).
